recipes.name: Quick Savory Cranberry Glazed Pork Loin Roast
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.5 ounce) can whole berry cranberry sauce

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Combine the cranberry sauce, apple jelly, mustard, crushed bouillon, horseradish, garlic powder, and thyme in a saucepan; bring to a boil.
Line a large baking pan with foil. Place pork loin in pan, fat side up. Sprinkle evenly with salt and pepper. Use a pastry brush and a small spoon to completely coat the pork with sauce.

Cook until the pork is no longer pink in the center, and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center reads 145 degrees F (63 degrees C), about 45 minutes, basting every 10 minutes with remaining sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick Savory Cranberry Glazed Pork Loin Roast
raw_recipe.description: A basting sauce made with apple jelly, cranberry sauce, mustard, and horseradish helps make a terrific pork loin for any family gathering.

review.reviewBody: Very tasty pork roast. I found the time/temp a little off. Pork should be cooked to 140-145 degrees and then set aside to rest for 15 minutes; the internal temp will go up and the juices will seep throughout the meat. A foolproof rule of thumb to use is 15 minutes per pound @ 350 degrees. In my experience, cooking to an internal temp of 160 or above usually results in unpleasantly dry meat. For succulence, give my suggestion a try.

Delicious. I too let the roast get to room temp prior to cooking. Used dried thyme and peach preserves. Don't love cubed bouillon so used one pack chicken flavor enhancer by Swansons. Increased horseradish a tad. Was superb cooked to 145. I just made the sauce on the stove top and chopped up half onion to it as well. Split it to serve half and use half to glaze. There was plenty. Foil in bottom of pan helps with cleanup as the sugar in the jelly can blacken in the pan. Will make often. Thank you for the great recipe!!!

Very good! I didn't have time to cook as directed. I just threw it into the crock pot on low for about 6-7 hours, put a little cranberry sauce under the meat, sprinkled all the ingredients on top of the pork (just a sprinkle of powdered chicken bullion and no horseradish), along with the rest of the cranberry and maybe half a cup of grape jelly (I didn't have apple). The flavor was great. The sauce it made was extremely tasty. I am sure baking as directed is even better, but if your in a rush, this still works out great. My family loved it.

I, like someone else, made it in the crock pot after browning it on all sides. I also substituted orange marmalade for the Apple jelly. My guests raved! Making it again for a luncheon with 30 ladies this week. Will post photos then!

My hubby made this last night and it was really good. We cooked the pork until it was 145 degrees F, because if you cook it more than that it will probably taste dry (The lastest from the FDA states it's ok to cook pork to 140- 145 degrees F and still be safe). We never cook pork more than 145 degrees F and it does make a difference in how delicious and moist it is. Remove from oven and let meat rest for 10 minutes. It was so moist and delicious and you could cut it with a fork! We did double the sauce and used 1/2 for baking and basting and 1/2 (keeping separate from the basting one) for pouring over individual servings. The cranberries that are baked are kind of crunchy and delicious! My 3 year old grandson who doesn't like a lot of meat, devoured it (and requested more sauce on his serving). This is definitely a keeper! We will be making this one often. The only change we made was to double the sauce and that's it.

I cooked on the green egg
Indirect at 425 took about 1:30 min
Gave it a smoky flavor second time I made it everyone loved it really juicy

Delicious! Didn't have a lot of time for the prep, so I just mixed the sauce all together and heated it up before putting it in the crockpot. Cooked it on high for 4 hours (should have checked it earlier, but was busy and forgot). Cooked it 10 degrees too long, but irregardless it was perfect! Will definitely keep this recipe on hand, especially if the President stops by! My son said he thought it was "festive" ... he's 34 and loved it. I thickened the sauce and used it for gravy and served it over the mashed potatoes. Yummy!

This was the best recipe I've ever used for pork! I agree with some other reviews that the sauce smelled a little weird while it was boiling, but by the time I poured it onto the pork and they started cooking together, the smells blended nicely. I didn't have fresh thyme, so I used dried. I stabbed the pork with a knife a few times so the sauce would work its way in. I peeled and sliced a granny smith apple to arrange around the pork in the pan, and cooked it covered for 40 minutes and uncovered for 20 more at 350. I basted it a few times while it was uncovered, and prepared mashed potatoes and green beans as side dishes. DELICIOUS MEAL! I had some extra sauce when the pork was gone, and I used it on leftover turkey too. So good!

This was really good!! I left out the horseradish cause I didn't have any available. I used homemade cranberry sauce and homemade apple jelly. I also used a slow-cooker on high for 4 hours cause my oven broke down. It was amazing! My husband went for seconds, the kids cleaned their plates and my bro in law told my sis to take some notes on how to make! Will do again!!

After reading the recipe, I knew my family would love it. However, once I was committed, I discovered it wasn't a loin cut that was thawed and I didn't have all the ingredients I thought I did. I read through a lot of the reviews and got an idea of compromises/substitutions I could use. So, here is what I did. 
 I used cranberry jelly, homemade peach jam, deli-style mustard, chicken base, prepared wasabi, 2 tsp. garlic powder, 1 tsp. dried thyme, pork sirloin roast (3 pieces equaling 6.7#). Tied roasts. 425*Fan for 12 min. Reduce temp to 325*Fan and baste every 12 min. Took about a full hour to cook. Even my reluctant pork eater gobbled it up. WINNER, WINNER, PORK ROAST DINNER!

made this last night and it was, and I quote, "Amazing!"

I cooked it at 350 for about an hour until the thermometer read 145 and I let it rest for a good fifteen minutes.

I did not baste the roast every 10 minutes, though, as it would mess with the oven temp. I didn't really need to baste it, though, as the sauce stayed on the meat the whole time.

I put celery, potatoes, and carrots in the roasting pan along w/ the pork roast.

The sauce is amazing! I will definitely make just the sauce again to serve with other meals. Yum!
I made this recipie for 60 people. I got 5 stars from my eaters. I was asked for the recipie at least a dozen times. Its' easy enough to make it a monthly dinner night. I wouldn't change a thing.
I liked but seems to be missing something Maybe a little brown sugar?
I think my roast was bigger than theirs because it took 2 hours with basting every 10 minutes. Also, I didn’t have apple jelly so I used orange marmalade but it was still good.

Loved it! Had to sub orange marmalade for the apple jelly. Then, browned the roast first. Put it in the roasting pan lined with foil, then wrapped the foil around the roast. 350 for 50 minutes or so, but check before. 140, then let it rest for 15 minutes. Moist and gooood.

Great recipe! I couldn’t find Apple Jelly, so I used Orange Marmalade instead. Followed the rest of the recipe exactly, except cooked in a roaster at 350. It was a big hit, so yummy! It’s going on my rotation list!
This is excellent. I made it exactly as the recipe reads and it is so amazing! Totally worth making, a great dish for holidays and company. It was a big hit!
I am allergic to horseradish. I subbed the apple jelly for a pepper apple jelly and added cayenne pepper for the kick... other then that followed and delicious!’
Delicious! I had to substitute sweet orange jelly for the apple jelly, and it worked out well. Next time I will add more dijon and horseradish for a little more kick.
Like Paula, I found that the timing was off a bit. I had to leave it in an extra 20 minutes and ended up with some pink deep in the roast. I’m thinking to let it set for 15 minutes
